html:
In late 2017 an outbreak of plague spread through the cities of Madagascar, including Antananarivo, infecting over two thousand people and killing about two hundred.

Plague has been present in Madagascar since it arrived by ship in 1898, carried by rats and fleas, and cases occur every year in the highlands. This outbreak was unusual because most cases were of the pneumonic form, which spreads from person to person by coughing, in towns.

With help from the World Health Organization, the government treated contacts with antibiotics and closed schools, and the outbreak ended by November. It drew warnings against handling the dead at famadihana and showed the weakness of health care in Madagascar, among the oldest plague strongholds remaining.
sum: In late 2017 an outbreak of plague spread through the cities of Madagascar, including Antananarivo, infecting over two thousand people and killing about two hundred.
